basis: Lysosomal storage disease group explicitly defined by mental disability and skeletal malformations; additional organ damage varies by subtype.

decisions.neurologic: primary: mental disability is explicitly part of the disease group's definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal malformations are explicitly part of the disease group's definition.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; airway malacia 2/2, urinary obstruction 1/1 and hearing impairment 1/1 support involvement, although samples are small. Cardiac prevalence is uncertain.

decisions.renal: involved: ureteral stenosis and hydronephrosis each reported in 1/1 assessed; obstructive urinary malformations are recognized syndrome features, with small-sample uncertainty.

basis: Inherited prion neurodegeneration; dysautonomia, dysphagia and sleep apnea reflect neural dysfunction rather than direct damage to additional organs.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inherited PRNP-associated protein misfolding causes this disease; potential prion transmissibility does not establish an infectious etiology in affected families.

basis: Familial PRP is an immune-mediated inflammatory keratinization disorder affecting skin and nails; ocular and oral abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: familial PRP has an autoinflammatory, immune-mediated cutaneous mechanism involving dysregulated CARD14 signaling.

basis: Parasitic lymphatic infection with defining elephantiasis of skin/subcutis; hyperkeratosis occurs in 30-79%. Renal and pulmonary abnormalities are below 30%.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: chronic enlargement and thickening of skin/subcutis constitute the named elephantiasis phenotype; hyperkeratosis occurs in 30-79%.

basis: Cauda equina nerve compression or injury; bowel and bladder symptoms arise from denervation and do not establish direct visceral damage.

decisions.renal: none: common bladder dysfunction reflects sacral nerve injury; direct urinary tract damage is not established as a common defining manifestation.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: bowel control dysfunction reflects sacral denervation rather than direct disease of the gastrointestinal tract.

basis: Developmental and intellectual impairment characterize 9p duplication syndromes; digital hypoplasia and skeletal malformations occur in >30% across typical presentations.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: digital hypoplasia and other skeletal malformations commonly accompany the developmental phenotype, affecting an estimated >30% across the spectrum.

basis: Vertebral fusion and congenital myopathy define the syndrome; persistent ptosis occurs in 2/2. Microcephaly alone does not establish CNS damage; cardiomyopathy frequency is unknown.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 2/2 does not alone establish brain dysfunction; motor delay and hypotonia can be explained by the defining congenital myopathy.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; developmental impairment and caudate atrophy in 2/2 establish neurologic damage. Scoliosis accompanies spasticity; diaphragm aplasia is an isolated report.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability, movement disorders and caudate atrophy occur in 2/2; these are direct consequences of the metabolic defect.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis in 2/2 accompanies severe spasticity; diaphragm aplasia in one assessed patient does not establish direct muscle or skeletal disease in >=30% overall.

basis: Poliosis, septal defect and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; respiratory abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with bronchomalacia reported. Ocular dysfunction at 30-79% is omitted by cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: respiratory abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with bronchomalacia reported; retained under the cap because involvement is more frequent than ocular dysfunction.
decisions.ocular: none under cap: myopia and strabismus occur in 30-79% and qualify, but pulmonary involvement is more frequent; blue sclera alone does not establish functional damage.
